content_universe: Pixel & Ink Studio — Andrés, Sophia (AD), Laura (SM). Bogotá, 6 meses de experiencia. Cliente: La Esquina Bakery (panadería de barrio, 20 años, audiencia familiar). Brief en tránsito: Andrés debe responder a Sophia por email confirmando decisiones de tipografía + color + entregables.
derived_from: pm-1-2.json (G1 toolbelt 20 terms, functions F1-F5, CEFR A1.1 descriptors)
pm-2-3.json (Master Anchor Text — serif vs sans-serif article)
pm-0-context.json (§5 SUCCESS, §9.1 L1 20% S3, §9.2 Grammar max 2 Intro)

pm0_anchor.feedback_mode_dominant: Elicitation + Recast (focus on form during editing, meaning during production)
success_factors_applied: Salience (chunks highlighted in color on Language Bank)
Use (immediate productive use — Andrés writes real email)
Connection (every chunk tied to Toolbelt from PM-2.3)
Context (authentic workplace scenario — client brief response)
Emotion (tied to Andrés's Monday panic relieved by structured template)
Spaced repetition (vocab recycled from S2 Reading + Vocab)
Synergy (Reading → Writing: same Toolbelt, same universe)

universe_anchor.protagonist_action_s3: Andrés must write a Design Decision Email to Sophia confirming his choices for La Esquina Bakery: font family (serif — Playfair Display), color palette (warm — brown + cream), and logo concept (round seal with wheat icon). Email is the product of S3.
universe_anchor.genre: Professional Design Decision Email (To: AD / From: Junior / Re: Client Brief Response)
universe_anchor.register: Semi-formal professional (intern → art director internal email)
universe_anchor.model_source: Master Anchor Text genre extension — same vocabulary universe, different skill mode
universe_anchor.integrates_with_s4: Andrés will later READ a recorded voice note from Sophia responding to his email (PM-2.6 Listening)

bilingual_unified_header.english: WRITING WORKSHOP — You are Andrés. Sophia is waiting for your email. Turn your design decisions into words.
bilingual_unified_header.spanish_italics: (Eres Andrés. Sophia espera tu email. Convierte tus decisiones de diseño en palabras.)
bilingual_unified_header.motivational_hook: Tuesday morning, 9:00 AM. Coffee. Laptop. One email. You can do this.

blueprint_model.title: 📝 THE BLUEPRINT MODEL — Design Decision Email Anatomy
blueprint_model.genre_analysis_of_master_anchor: The Master Anchor Text (PM-2.3) taught you the CONCEPTS (serif vs sans-serif, warm vs cool). Now you use those concepts in a REAL professional genre: the internal design email.

move_structure.register_note: First name + comma = semi-formal (same office, close colleague)

move_structure.example_from_universe: This is the brief for La Esquina Bakery.
The font is Playfair Display. The colors are brown and cream. The logo is a round seal.
move_structure.function: Describe technical choices (F2 — Give information + F3 — Describe)
move_structure.grammar_target: Article + noun + be + descriptor (Gr3 + Gr1 + Gr4)

move_structure.example_from_universe: The bakery is 20 years old. Warm colors are friendly.
move_structure.function: Justify choice (F4 — Express opinion, light scaffolding)

move_structure.register_note: Please = polite marker. Thanks, + name = standard sign-off.

anti_model_warning.label: ⚠️ AVOID
anti_model_warning.bad_example: Hey!! so the font is like, you know, the old-style one?? colors are yellow-brown-ish idk. peace ✌️
anti_model_warning.why_it_fails: Informal slang + vague terms + no concrete decisions + emoji. This is a chat message, not a design email.
anti_model_warning.spanish: (Evita: lenguaje informal, términos vagos, sin decisiones concretas.)

language_bank.title: 🔧 LANGUAGE BANK — 8 Reusable Chunks
language_bank.instruction: Copy these into your email. Change ONE word to fit your decision.
language_bank.spanish: (Copia estos bloques en tu email. Cambia UNA palabra para adaptarlos a tu decisión.)

chunks.variation_example: This is the brief for La Esquina Bakery.
The colors are brown and cream.
The logo is a round seal.
My client is a family bakery.

archetypes_integrated.policy: ALL 5 archetypes A-E are documented with full PRE/DURING/POST. Instructor picks one flow per session. All flows produce E2 Writing (5 pts) — a complete Design Decision Email.
archetypes_integrated.spanish: (TODOS los 5 arquetipos están documentados. El instructor elige un flujo por sesión. Todos producen la misma evidencia E2.)

archetype_A_exploratory.name: Exploratory Writing — Quickwrite → Expand
archetype_A_exploratory.when_it_works: When learners freeze at the blank page; when fluency matters more than accuracy.
archetype_A_exploratory.fit_for_A1_1: High — removes anxiety; ideal starting archetype for first writing task in the program.

activities.instruction_bilingual: Set a 5-minute timer. Write non-stop. No grammar worries. (*Cronómetro 5 min. Escribe sin parar. No te preocupes por la gramática.*)
prompts_3_options: What are the colors and font for La Esquina Bakery?
Why are warm colors good for a bakery?
What is your logo? Describe it in simple words.
activities.rule: Minimum 40 words. Any word counts. Spanish words allowed IF you don't know the English.

activities.instruction_bilingual: Write TWO short quickwrites on two different prompts. (*Escribe DOS quickwrites cortos sobre dos prompts diferentes.*)
activities.structure: Quickwrite 1: 5 min on Prompt 1. | Quickwrite 2: 5 min on Prompt 2. | 10 min: share both with partner; partner circles favorite sentence.
activities.teacher_move: Do NOT correct grammar. Encourage quantity. Circulate with supportive nods only.

activities.phase: POST-WRITING — Select + Expand into Email (20 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Pick your best quickwrite. Turn it into a proper email using the Blueprint Model. (*Elige tu mejor quickwrite. Conviértelo en un email usando el Blueprint Model.*)
steps: 1. Read both quickwrites. Which has your best idea?
2. Use the Blueprint Model (5 moves) to restructure.
4. Run the Auditor's Checklist before submitting.
activities.evidence: The expanded email = E2 Writing (5 pts).

archetype_B_academic_formal.name: Academic/Formal Writing — Mentor Text + Structured Email
archetype_B_academic_formal.when_it_works: When the programa técnico demands professional output; when precision matters.
archetype_B_academic_formal.fit_for_A1_1: Stretch — requires scaffolded sentence frames. Works with HEAVY support.

activities.instruction_bilingual: Read the sample email. Highlight the 5 moves. (*Lee el email modelo. Resalta los 5 movimientos.*)
activities.mentor_text_sample: Hi Sophia, | This is the brief for Café Luna. | The font is Montserrat. The colors are black and gold. The logo is a crescent moon. | The café is modern. Cool colors are elegant. | Please review. Thanks, Andrés.
analysis_questions: 1. Which sentences are the GREETING and CLOSING?
4. What register is used? (formal / semi-formal / informal)

activities.phase: DURING WRITING — Structured Production with Frames (20 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Write your email for La Esquina Bakery using EVERY sentence frame. (*Escribe tu email para La Esquina Bakery usando CADA marco de oración.*)
activities.grammar_focus: Article placement (Gr3) + adjective before noun (Gr4) + be conjugation (Gr1).

activities.phase: POST-WRITING — Peer Review with Rubric (15 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Exchange emails with a partner. Score with the rubric. Give 1 specific suggestion. (*Intercambia emails con un compañero. Puntúa con la rúbrica. Da 1 sugerencia específica.*)

archetype_C_collaborative_tblt.name: Collaborative TBLT — Team Email in Roles
archetype_C_collaborative_tblt.when_it_works: When negotiation of meaning matters; when the workplace is collaborative by nature (design studios ARE team environments).
archetype_C_collaborative_tblt.fit_for_A1_1: High — distributes cognitive load across team; perfect for first-time writers.

activities.phase: PRE-WRITING — Scenario Briefing + Role Assignment (10 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: You are the Pixel & Ink Studio team. Sophia needs ONE email from all of you. Assign roles. (*Ustedes son el equipo del estudio. Sophia necesita UN email de todos. Asignen roles.*)
activities.scenario: It's Tuesday. Sophia has a client call at 11 AM with La Esquina Bakery. She needs the brief response BEFORE the call.

roles_for_teams_of_3.responsibility: Writes the email draft using Language Bank chunks.
roles_for_teams_of_3.spanish: (Escribe el borrador usando los bloques del Language Bank.)

roles_for_teams_of_3.responsibility: Checks register and word count; smooths transitions.
roles_for_teams_of_3.spanish: (Revisa el registro y el conteo de palabras; suaviza transiciones.)

roles_for_teams_of_3.responsibility: Runs the Auditor's Checklist; confirms 5 chunks + 5 moves.
roles_for_teams_of_3.spanish: (Corre el Auditor's Checklist; confirma 5 chunks + 5 movimientos.)

activities.phase: DURING WRITING — Collaborative Production on Shared Document (25 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Open Google Doc. Write together. Negotiate each choice aloud in English. (*Abran Google Doc. Escriban juntos. Negocien cada elección en voz alta en inglés.*)
negotiation_prompts: Is 'friendly' a good rationale or too simple?
Do we need a second color or is one enough?
activities.output_format: Single shared document; all 3 members type; Verifier reads aloud each sentence before it's final.

activities.instruction_bilingual: Each team tapes their email to the wall. Walk around. Vote for the strongest email. (*Cada equipo pega su email en la pared. Recorran. Voten por el email más fuerte.*)
activities.evaluation_criteria: Clearest decisions + best register + most natural chunks.
activities.reflection: 1 minute: What did we negotiate? Why did we change that word?

archetype_D_ai_mediated.name: AI-Mediated Writing — Draft → AI-Check → Critical Edit
archetype_D_ai_mediated.when_it_works: When the programa técnico includes modern tools (MGV = digital design — AI is part of the workflow); when prompt literacy is a transferable competency.
archetype_D_ai_mediated.fit_for_A1_1: Stretch — requires tech access + strong teacher presence. Powerful if available.
archetype_D_ai_mediated.tech_required: ChatGPT, Copilot, or Gemini (free tier) + laptops or phones

activities.phase: PRE-WRITING — Solo Draft WITHOUT AI (15 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Close all tabs. No AI yet. Write your email draft alone. (*Cierra todas las pestañas. Sin IA aún. Escribe tu borrador solo.*)
activities.rule: This first draft is YOURS. The AI will help LATER, not NOW. The goal is to see what YOU can do.
activities.output: Handwritten or typed draft, 60-80 words, 5 moves.

activities.phase: DURING WRITING — Targeted AI Consultation (20 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Use the AI for ONE specific check only. (*Usa la IA para UN chequeo específico solamente.*)

prompt_literacy_templates.prompt_template: I am a beginner English learner (A1). Is this sentence correct? If not, explain the error in simple words: [paste your sentence]
prompt_literacy_templates.expected_interaction: You accept or reject the AI correction + write WHY in your reflective journal.

prompt_literacy_templates.prompt_template: I am writing a semi-formal email. Give me 3 polite ways to close: 'Please review. Thanks.' — are there alternatives at A1 level?
prompt_literacy_templates.expected_interaction: You pick ONE and justify in 1 sentence.

prompt_literacy_templates.prompt_template: Is 'friendly' the right word to describe warm colors? Give 2 alternative A1-level words.
prompt_literacy_templates.expected_interaction: You pick word that best fits your bakery + explain why.

reflective_journal_prompts: What did the AI suggest that I didn't think of?
What did the AI suggest that was WRONG or too advanced?
What did I keep from my original draft? Why?

activities.phase: POST-WRITING — Final Human Edit + Critical Reflection (15 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: The final email is YOURS. Compare solo draft vs AI-influenced version. Which moves are stronger? (*El email final es TUYO. Compara borrador solo vs versión con IA. ¿Qué movimientos son más fuertes?*)
critical_questions: Did the AI help me learn or did I copy?
If I write another email next week, can I do it without AI now?
What's 1 chunk I learned from this interaction?

archetype_E_genre_based.name: Genre-Based Writing — Analyze → Imitate → Transfer
archetype_E_genre_based.when_it_works: When the genre (professional email) is a lifelong transferable skill; when the learner needs to replicate the genre in many future contexts.
archetype_E_genre_based.fit_for_A1_1: High — builds genre awareness that compounds across sessions; ideal if program values transferable workplace genres.

activities.phase: PRE-WRITING — Genre Analysis of 3 Email Samples (15 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Read these 3 emails. Fill the Genre Recipe chart. (*Lee estos 3 emails. Llena la receta del género.*)

sample_emails.label: Sample 1 — Café Luna
sample_emails.text: Hi Sophia, | This is the brief for Café Luna. | The font is Montserrat. The colors are black and gold. The logo is a crescent moon. | The café is modern. Cool colors are elegant. | Please review. Thanks, Andrés.

sample_emails.label: Sample 2 — Nova Bookshop
sample_emails.text: Hi Sophia, | This is the brief for Nova Bookshop. | The font is Garamond. The colors are navy and white. The logo is a flat book. | The bookshop is classic. Cool colors are calm. | Please review. Thanks, Andrés.

sample_emails.label: Sample 3 — GymStrong
sample_emails.text: Hi Sophia, | This is the brief for GymStrong. | The font is Bebas Neue. The colors are red and black. The logo is a bold triangle. | The gym is energetic. Warm colors are strong. | Please review. Thanks, Andrés.

activities.phase: DURING WRITING — Produce Email Following the Recipe (20 min)
activities.instruction_bilingual: Write YOUR email for La Esquina Bakery. Hit all 8 recipe slots. (*Escribe TU email para La Esquina Bakery. Cubre los 8 slots de la receta.*)
activities.scaffolding: Check off each slot as you complete it. Compare your text to Sample 1, 2, 3.
activities.peer_check: Partner verifies all 8 slots are present + asks one 'recipe' question.

activities.instruction_bilingual: Same recipe, NEW client. In 10 minutes: write the email for a client of YOUR choice. (*Misma receta, NUEVO cliente. En 10 min: escribe el email para un cliente de TU elección.*)
activities.reflection: Which parts of the recipe are FIXED (always the same)? Which are FREE (change per client)?
activities.meta_goal: Learner walks away knowing how to write ANY design decision email in the future — genre mastery achieved.

rotation_options_for_instructor.policy: Instructor picks ONE flow for the 50-minute block based on class energy, tech access, and course sequencing.
rotation_options_for_instructor.spanish: (El instructor elige UN flujo para el bloque de 50 min según la energía del grupo, el acceso a tecnología y la secuencia del curso.)

flows.name: First-Time Writers (A1.1 default)
flows.sequence: Archetype A (Exploratory) → students write without fear → expand best quickwrite into email
flows.best_for: Groups with high writing anxiety; first writing task in the program

flows.name: Formal-Professional Track
flows.sequence: Archetype B (Academic/Formal) → mentor text analysis → frames → peer review
flows.best_for: Groups that learn best with explicit models and structure

flows.name: Team-Based Workplace Simulation
flows.sequence: Archetype C (Collaborative TBLT) → role assignment → Google Doc → gallery walk
flows.best_for: Classes that thrive in groups; distributes cognitive load across team
flows.tech_needs: Laptops + Google Docs OR paper poster per team

flows.name: Tech-Forward Prompt Literacy
flows.sequence: Archetype D (AI-Mediated) → solo draft → targeted AI consultation → critical edit + journal
flows.best_for: Programs where digital tools are part of professional practice (MGV native fit)
flows.tech_needs: Laptops/phones + ChatGPT or equivalent (free tier ok)

flows.name: Transferable Genre Mastery (Recommended for G1)
flows.sequence: Archetype E (Genre-Based) → 3 samples → recipe → produce → transfer to new client
flows.best_for: When the goal is a skill that transfers across future situations (design briefs are forever)

flows.name: Maximalist Writing Rotation (Hybrid A+C+E)
flows.sequence: 15min Quickwrite warmup (A) → 20min Team Email (C) → 15min Transfer to new client (E)
flows.best_for: Extended 90-min block (S3 stretched); mixes fluency + collaboration + transfer

rotation_options_for_instructor.recommended_for_G1: FLOW-W5 — Genre-Based delivers the most transferable skill for design students; writing design briefs is part of every future client interaction.

auditors_checklist.title: 📋 THE AUDITOR'S CHECKLIST — Self-Review Before Submitting
auditors_checklist.instruction_bilingual: Before you hand in the email, check each box. (*Antes de entregar el email, marca cada casilla.*)

criteria.description: I copied at least 5 of the 8 chunks (with adaptations)
No slang, no emojis, no chat-style
Count before submitting — not too short, not too long

auditors_checklist.self_score_key: 5/5 = Ready to submit | 4/5 = Fix 1 thing | 3/5 or less = Revisit one activity

rubric_visible_to_learner.title: 📊 VISIBLE RUBRIC — E2 Writing (5 pts total)
rubric_visible_to_learner.instruction_bilingual: This is how your instructor will grade the email. (*Así te calificará el instructor.*)

criteria.excellent: All 5 moves present and in order

criteria.criterion: Grammar (Gr1 be + Gr2 pronouns/demos + Gr3 a/an + Gr4 adjective position)
criteria.adequate: Minor errors but message is clear

criteria.excellent: Font + color + shape + product terms all used accurately
criteria.incipient: Few Toolbelt terms or used incorrectly

criteria.excellent: Semi-formal throughout; decisions are crystal clear

rubric_visible_to_learner.cuestionario_contribution: 5 items worth 1 pt each will appear in S6 Cuestionario Consolidado (Writing section)

tres_versiones.apropiacion_s3: E2 Writing Task — Design Decision Email (5 pts formal evidence with rubric)
tres_versiones.evaluacion_s6: 5 items in Writing section of Cuestionario Consolidado (1 pt each, 5 pts total Writing)
tres_versiones.autonomia_workbook: REINFORCE: same chunks with new client. EXTEND: write response to an angry client (HOTS). PREPARE: read sample before S4 Listening.

cuestionario_items_harvest_preview.note: Items generated here feed PM-4.2 Cuestionario S6 Writing section (5 items × 1 pt).

sample_items.stem: Which sentence gives a DECISION (not rationale)?
options: c) The font is Playfair Display.
d) The bakery is 20 years old.

sample_items.stem: Which closing fits a semi-formal email?

feedback.dominant_mode: Elicitation during production + Recast during editing
accuracy_techniques: Frame-by-frame error highlighting on peer review
Targeted recast on adjective position (Gr4) and article (Gr3) errors
fluency_techniques: Quickwrite (Archetype A) — no interruption during writing
Reflective journal (Archetype D) — fluency of thought about process

l1_management.english_zone: Activated during DURING WRITING phases; allowed during PRE (brainstorming) and POST (reflection)
legitimate_L1_uses: Clarifying rubric criteria when learner freezes
Negotiating meaning in Archetype C role assignments
Reflecting in Archetype D journal (journal can be bilingual)
l1_management.reduction_strategy: S3 is 20% → S4 will drop to 15% as speaking picks up

physical_techniques: Tap desk on stressed syllable while reading email aloud
Mark stress with a dot above the vowel in the final draft
stress_pronunciation.board_marking: Write 5 focus words; mark stressed syllable with dot; students copy into their email draft before reading

factors_applied.Salience: Language Bank chunks color-coded on worksheet
factors_applied.Connection: Every term tied to Toolbelt from PM-2.3
factors_applied.Emotion: Tied to Andrés's relief once email is sent
factors_applied.Spaced_repetition: Terms recycled from S2 Reading + S2 Vocabulary
factors_applied.Synergy: Reading → Writing → Vocabulary Word Wall — same universe

integration_all_archetypes_policy.rationale: Per Sergio's directive (2026-04-20): 'Quiero todos los arquetipos para todos los PM.' All 5 archetypes are documented. Instructor rotates flows across cohorts or sessions.
integration_all_archetypes_policy.recommended_default_for_G1: FLOW-W5 (Genre-Based) — because learning the design decision email genre is a lifelong ESP skill for MGV graduates.
integration_all_archetypes_policy.workbook_use: The 5 archetypes also populate PM-3.4 Workbook: 1 archetype per Workbook chapter extension activity.

activities.statement: Redactar un email de decisión de diseño (60-80 palabras) para un cliente del universo Pixel & Ink Studio, aplicando los 5 movimientos del género (greeting, context, decisions, rationale, closing), mínimo 5 chunks del Language Bank y las estructuras gramaticales Gr1-Gr4.
activities.didactic_technique: Taller de escritura con andamiaje por género

activities.statement: Revisar y editar el email usando el Auditor's Checklist de 5 criterios y la rúbrica visible, aplicando auto-corrección y (si el arquetipo es C) peer review para asegurar registro semi-formal y precisión en estructuras gramaticales.
activities.didactic_technique: Análisis de casos + Revisión por pares

evidence.description: El aprendiz produce un email de decisión de diseño de 60-80 palabras en inglés técnico, demostrando control de Gr1 (be), Gr2 (pronouns/demos), Gr3 (a/an), Gr4 (adjective position), vocabulario del Toolbelt (10 términos mínimo) y organización por 5 movimientos del género.

C_collaborative_tblt: Laptops con Google Docs O papel de cartel por equipo

always_required: Master Anchor Text de PM-2.3 como referencia
environment.instructors: Instructor de inglés técnico (con apoyo opcional de instructor técnico si arquetipo C requiere validación de decisiones de diseño)

ambiente_learning.configuration: Mesas de 3 personas (ideal para Arquetipo C); individual para A/B/D/E
ambiente_learning.equipment: Proyector para mentor text (B/E); wifi para D; pared para gallery walk (C); Word Wall ya establecido desde S2
ambiente_learning.conditions: Iluminación adecuada para escritura; silencio durante Quickwrite (A); voz media durante negociación (C)

estrategia_didactica.estrategia: Aprendizaje Basado en Tareas (TBLT) con Writing Workshop Approach
estrategia_didactica.justificacion: S3 es sesión de producción escrita; la tarea concreta (email profesional) ancla el aprendizaje en un contexto laboral real del universo MGV.

tecnicas_por_arquetipo.B: Análisis de mentor text + sentence frames

cognitiva_saber.objeto: la estructura de 5 movimientos del email de decisión de diseño
cognitiva_saber.condicion: analizando mentor texts y completando el genre recipe

procedimental_hacer.objeto: un email de decisión de diseño de 60-80 palabras con Gr1-Gr4 y ≥10 términos del Toolbelt
procedimental_hacer.condicion: siguiendo el arquetipo seleccionado y aplicando la rúbrica visible

actitudinal_ser.objeto: rol profesional de diseñador junior comunicando decisiones técnicas al cliente interno
actitudinal_ser.condicion: manteniendo registro semi-formal y respetando convenciones del género email

checks_internos.check: CEFR A1.1 ceiling respetado (chunks simples, sentence frames heavy, 60-80 palabras)
Integración de TODOS los 5 arquetipos A-E con PRE/DURING/POST completos

§5 Feedback differentiated (accuracy during editing, fluency during production)
§6 A1.1 descriptors respected (can write short simple emails with frames)
